native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber had its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE, peaking in the interval ~3300-3000 BCE (z = 1.54, the dataset maximum), after a sustained high phase at z = 1.46 from ~4000 BCE; after the peak, amber declined sharply at the 3rd-millennium transition and never recovered.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 yearly rows, CE -4100..-500, BCE as negative CE), capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300-500, comma decimals), and the pollen PC1 file (convention check only). Verified Amber_inter is linear interpolation of the 37 raw Amber anchors (100-yr steps) which exactly match capital.csv Zamber. Binned by millennium BCE (4th mil = 4000-3001 BCE): 4th-millennium bin has the highest mean (+1.49) and shares the global max (1.54). Peak plateau = contiguous span where Amber_inter equals the global max (BCE 3300-3000, reported at 100-year anchor resolution); high phase = raw anchors z>=1.46 (BCE 4000-3000). Cross-checked against capital.csv (max Zamber 1.54, group MN, BCE 3300; extra BCE 4300/4200 rows do not change the result). Disclosed the 5th-millennium interpolation edge artifact. Script: analysis_amber_peak.py; outputs: output/amber_peak_results.json.
